source_resources.author: Stanford University CS336 Staff
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: tests/test_serialization.py: test_checkpointing; model, optimizer and iteration state
source_resources.version_or_verification_date: spring2025 tag; README, tests and MIT LICENSE checked 2026-11-01
source_resources.permission_basis: External hyperlink only to the spring2025 assignment repository; its LICENSE is MIT. No assignment text, code or lecture material is imported.
source_resources.prerequisites: Fluent Python, PyTorch, and linear algebra
source_resources.selection_rationale: Lead assignment-driven source for pretraining component practice and tests. nanoGPT remains a compact historical code-reading companion, not the current recommended training curriculum.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Public tagged handout and tests; full training needs suitable compute. The campus cluster is not required for reading or local component practice.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Local self-contained pretraining scripts run on standard local CPUs or budget GPUs without Stanford cluster dependency.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Simpler code layout, useful complementary reference for minimal PyTorch Transformer.
High-level API focus rather than building from raw tensor fundamentals.

source_resources.title: PyTorch Tutorial: Saving and Loading Models
source_resources.author: PyTorch Documentation Team
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under BSD open source documentation license.
source_resources.prerequisites: Python, PyTorch tensors and nn.Module basics.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Official documentation detailing state_dict serialization, optimizer state saving, and safe loading patterns.
source_resources.safe_fallback: All checkpoint serialization semantics, dictionary schema keys, and safe recovery steps are self-contained in lesson code.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: TensorFlow trackable checkpoint architecture; PyTorch's explicit dictionary is our target implementation standard.
Safetensors provides safe zero-copy tensor storage without pickle, compared directly when discussing pickle execution risks.

source_resources.title: nanoGPT: train.py pretraining loop
source_resources.author: Andrej Karpathy
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under MIT open source license.
source_resources.prerequisites: Transformer architecture from Days 46-48 and training loop from Days 49-51.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Compact historical code reference for the named implementation functions; CS336 spring2025 provides the lead component exercises. Do not infer top-p, atomic persistence or cloud budget enforcement from nanoGPT.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Historical implementation reference: nanoGPT README marks the repository deprecated (November 2025). Toy CPU reading/runs do not establish full GPU pretraining feasibility.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Complete checkpoint saving patterns and resuming loops are directly implemented in lesson exercises.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: High-complexity multi-GPU distributed model-parallel checkpointing; nanoGPT provides accessible single-GPU clarity.
High-level framework callback abstraction; nanoGPT keeps explicit control over state dict dictionaries.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: train.py: checkpoint dict {'model', 'optimizer', 'model_args', 'iter_num', 'best_val_loss', 'config'} written with torch.save to out_dir/ckpt.pt; the init_from == 'resume' branch reloads it
